questions.topic: Software that interprets HTML
questions.why: A web browser reads the HTML code of a page and displays it. Compilers and assemblers translate program code into machine code; they do not display web pages.

questions.topic: Number of cells in a spreadsheet range
questions.why: The range runs over 5 columns (A, B, C, D, E) and 5 rows (1 to 5), so it has 5 × 5 = 25 cells.

questions.topic: Binary subtraction
questions.why: Convert to decimal to check: 10101₂ = 21 and 1111₂ = 15. 21 − 15 = 6, and 6 in 4-bit binary is 0110.

questions.topic: Control structure that repeats steps
questions.why: Iteration (a loop) repeats a block of instructions. Sequence runs steps one after another; selection chooses between paths.

questions.topic: Check that data was received correctly
questions.why: A parity check adds an extra bit so the receiver can detect whether bits were changed during transmission. Format and length checks are for data entry, not transmission.

questions.topic: Boosting a weak signal
questions.why: A repeater receives a weak signal, regenerates it and sends it on at full strength, so it can travel further.

questions.topic: Type of software a DBMS is
questions.why: A database management system (such as MS Access) is used to carry out a user task, storing and querying data, so it is application software, not system software.

questions.topic: Malware hidden inside a genuine-looking program
questions.why: A Trojan horse pretends to be useful, legitimate software while hiding harmful code. A virus attaches to files and a worm spreads by itself across networks.

questions.topic: Computer with the highest throughput
questions.why: Two cores at 1.1 GHz can do about 2.2 GHz of work in parallel, and 4 GB is the most RAM (the maximum a 32-bit system can use). Option D runs at only 500 Hz, which is extremely slow.

questions.topic: Storage units from smallest to largest
questions.why: Bit < Byte (8 bits) < Kilobyte (1024 bytes) < Terabyte.

questions.topic: All computers connected to one central computer
questions.why: The computer in the control room acts as the server and the café computers are its clients: a client-server network. In peer-to-peer, all computers are equal.

questions.topic: NOT a feature of a good algorithm
questions.why: A good algorithm must be precise and unambiguous, finish in finite time and follow a logical order. Being ambiguous is the opposite of what is needed.

questions.topic: Domain name in a web address
questions.why: In https://www.cgceboard.cm/homepage.html, 'https' is the protocol, 'www' is the host, 'cgceboard.cm' is the domain name and 'homepage.html' is the file (page).

questions.topic: Sending images over telephone lines
questions.why: A fax (facsimile) machine scans a document or image and sends it over a telephone line to another fax machine, which prints it.

questions.topic: Identify the gate from its truth table
questions.why: The output is 1 only when the two inputs are different (0,1 and 1,0) and 0 when they are the same. That is the XOR (exclusive OR) gate.

questions.topic: Flowchart symbol for input/output
questions.why: The parallelogram is used for input and output. The rectangle is a process, the diamond is a decision and the rounded shape (oval) is start/stop.

questions.topic: Meaning of ATM
questions.why: ATM stands for Automated Teller Machine.

questions.topic: 'Wrong date and time' at start-up
questions.why: The date, time and BIOS settings are kept in CMOS memory, powered by a small battery. When the CMOS battery fails, the computer forgets the date and time.

questions.topic: Type of construct 'If – Then – Else' is
questions.why: If–Then–Else chooses between two paths depending on a condition, so it is selection (decision).

questions.topic: Circuit made of an OR gate followed by a NOT gate
questions.why: The OR gate's output goes into a NOT gate (the triangle with the small circle), which inverts it. NOT-OR is the NOR gate.

questions.topic: Polite behaviour on the Internet
questions.why: Netiquette (net + etiquette) is the set of rules for respectful behaviour online.

questions.topic: System that stores knowledge and imitates human reasoning
questions.why: An expert system holds the knowledge of human experts in a knowledge base and uses rules to reason and give advice, like a doctor or engineer would.

questions.topic: Person responsible for time and quality of a project
questions.why: The project manager plans the project, follows its schedule and budget, and makes sure it is delivered on time with acceptable quality.

questions.topic: A disadvantage of telebanking
questions.why: Options A and B are advantages. Because the account is reached over a network, a real disadvantage is the risk of accounts being hacked.

questions.topic: Concentric rings on a magnetic disk
questions.why: Tracks are the concentric circles on the disk surface. Each track is divided into sectors.

questions.topic: Using a new system alongside the old one
questions.why: Parallel running means the old and new systems are used at the same time until the new one is trusted. Direct changeover replaces the old system at once.

questions.topic: A key advantage of social networks
questions.why: Social networks let users share rich media (photos, audio and video) instantly with many people. Informal language is not an advantage, and large file transfer is not their purpose.

questions.topic: File a video program can open
questions.why: The extension .avi is a video format. .jpeg is an image, and .wav and .mp3 are audio files.

questions.topic: What a compiler is
questions.why: A compiler translates the whole source code of a high-level program into machine code (object code) before it is run.

questions.topic: Computer that processes discrete data
questions.why: Digital computers work with discrete values (0s and 1s). Analog computers use continuous data, and hybrid computers use both.

questions.topic: Units of time in increasing order
questions.why: 1 picosecond = 10⁻¹² s, 1 nanosecond = 10⁻⁹ s and 1 millisecond = 10⁻³ s, so picoseconds < nanoseconds < milliseconds.

questions.topic: What Android is
questions.why: Android is an operating system for smartphones and tablets, made by Google.

questions.topic: Component that says how operations are carried out
questions.why: Procedures are the rules and instructions that say how the people, hardware and software of an information system carry out each operation.

questions.topic: ASCII code of 'a' from the code of 'd'
questions.why: 01100100 = 100 in decimal. Letters are coded in order, and 'a' is 3 places before 'd', so 100 − 3 = 97 = 01100001.

questions.topic: Name for a web address
questions.why: A web address is a URL: Uniform Resource Locator.

questions.topic: Number of records for 150 students
questions.why: Each student is one record (one row), so 150 students give 150 records. The 5 headings are the fields (columns).

questions.topic: Hardware that emits more radiation
questions.why: CRT (cathode ray tube) monitors fire electron beams at the screen and give off more radiation than flat LCD screens.

questions.topic: Trying different values to see the effect
questions.why: Changing input values to see how the results change is what-if analysis, often done in a spreadsheet.

questions.topic: What a dual-core computer is
questions.why: A dual-core processor has two processing units on one chip, so it can process about twice as much data as a single core. It does not double the motherboard, system unit or memory.

questions.topic: Testing an algorithm with sample values
questions.why: A dry run means going through the algorithm by hand with test values (often using a trace table) to check that it gives the right result.

questions.topic: Hexadecimal CD to binary
questions.why: Convert each hex digit to 4 bits: C = 12 = 1100 and D = 13 = 1101, so CD₁₆ = 11001101₂.

questions.topic: How long a non-critical task can be delayed
questions.why: Slack (float) time is the time a task can be delayed without delaying the whole project. Tasks on the critical path have zero slack.

questions.topic: System that switches itself off and on by temperature
questions.why: The system reads the temperature and acts on it automatically (switching off at 80 °C, on below 50 °C). Acting on the readings makes it a control system; a monitoring system only records them.

questions.topic: NOT a physical (cable) medium
questions.why: Twisted-pair, coaxial and fibre-optic are cables (guided media). Microwaves travel through the air, so they are wireless (unguided) media.

questions.topic: Chart for managing a project from start to finish
questions.why: A Gantt chart shows each task as a bar against time, from the start to the end of a project.

questions.topic: Data type with only two values
questions.why: A Boolean holds only TRUE or FALSE (1 or 0).

questions.topic: Comments in a program
questions.why: Comments are notes for programmers. The compiler ignores them, so they are never compiled into the program.

questions.topic: Protecting archived files from unauthorised access
questions.why: Access to stored files is usually controlled with a password. Encryption also protects files, by making them unreadable without the key; antivirus and backups do not stop unauthorised access.

questions.topic: Interface where you click on commands
questions.why: A graphical user interface (GUI) lets the user click on icons, menus and buttons. A command line interface needs typed commands.

questions.topic: Device that splits one channel into many
questions.why: A demultiplexer takes one combined channel and splits it back into several. A multiplexer does the opposite: it combines several signals into one channel.
